meta.note: Question bank. Every answer traces to a real published statistic recorded in source/sourceUrl. kind: guess | text. finale: true marks the round-7 pool. Text rounds: textAnswers ranked list with accepted variants per rank, top1 is the #1 label (published only via Yesterday), unlisted are plausible strings that score as not on the list.

questions.text: What % of everyone alive today lives in Brazil?
questions.note: About 216 million Brazilians out of roughly 8.1 billion people on Earth.
questions.source: UN World Population Prospects 2024 (Worldometer): Brazil = 2.60% of world population in 2024 (exact published figure 2.6%; rounded to 3% for play — the game scores whole percentages)

questions.text: What % of US adults hold a PhD?
questions.note: Doctorates are rare everywhere.
questions.source: US Census Bureau, American Community Survey 2022: ~2% of US adults hold a doctoral degree

questions.text: What % of US households own a boat?
questions.source: National Marine Manufacturers Association / US Coast Guard: 11.9% of US households own a recreational boat

questions.text: What % of Iceland's population was not born in Iceland?

questions.text: Of all the pet dogs and cats in the US, what % are dogs?

questions.text: What % of people were born on February 29th?
questions.note: Leap day comes once every four years — roughly 1 birthday in 1,461.

questions.text: What % of people have perfect pitch?
questions.note: About 1 person in 10,000 can name a note with no reference.

questions.note: About two in three US households own their home.
questions.source: U.S. Census Bureau, Quarterly Residential Vacancies and Homeownership, Q2 2026: homeownership rate 65.0%

questions.text: What's the most common fear people have?

texts: Looking in the mirror at night

questions.source: YouGov US poll (2014, 1,000 US adults): snakes 64% at least a little afraid #1, heights 57% #2, public speaking 56% #3 — "Snakes, heights and public speaking are the top three fears in the Home of the Brave". Gallup (2001, 1,016 adults) agrees snakes #1 (51%). Chapman Survey of American Fears Wave 9 (2023) also ranks public speaking (28.7% afraid/very afraid) above insects/spiders (25.3%) among personal fears. RESOLVED: the n=2,088 poll that puts Heights #1 is YouGov GB, 18-19 Mar 2014 (Heights 58% total afraid, Public speaking 56%, Snakes 52%) — a British sample, not American. For this US-facing game the US poll governs, so Snakes stays #1; Spiders drops to #4 behind Public speaking per the US top three. No change below #4: no full published US ranking for the remaining fears could be verified.

questions.source: Moneypenny nationwide survey (published 28 Oct 2024, updated 2026): most common first jobs — Fast food 15% #1, Babysitting 12% #2, Retail 11% #3, Restaurant server 8% #4, Grocery store cashier 7% #5. questions.text: What % of all US web browsing happens on Google Chrome?

questions.text: What % of the world's people are left-handed?

questions.source: Papadatou-Pastou et al., Human handedness: A meta-analysis, Psychological Bulletin (2020) (exact published figure 10.6%; rounded to 11% for play — the game scores whole percentages)

questions.text: What % of babies born in the US are boys?

questions.text: What % of US workers drive to work alone?
questions.note: Census ACS 2024 Table B08301: 69.2% of US workers drove alone to work; the rest carpooled (9.2%), worked from home (13.3%), took transit (3.7%), walked or biked.
questions.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 2024, Table B08301

questions.text: What % of US adults own a smartphone?

questions.text: Name the most common pet people have
unlisted: a Tamagotchi (a toy, not a pet)
questions.source: APPA 2026 State of the Industry Report (released 26 Mar 2026, based on the 2025 National Pet Owners Survey): 95 million US households own a pet; Dog 71m households (53%) #1, Cat 53m (39%) #2, Freshwater fish 9m #3 (+ Saltwater fish 1m), Reptile 6m #4, Small animal 5m #5, Bird 5m #6, Horse 2m #7. Species breakdown as presented by APPA (APPA Instagram reel, May 2026) and corroborated by Spots / World Animal Foundation summaries of the same report. NOTE: Bird and Small animal are effectively tied at ~5m rounded; their order follows APPA's own presentation (small animal listed before bird). SUPERSEDED: the figures previously cited here (Dog 69.8m, Cat 49.2m, Fish 11.9m, Bird 6.9m, Small mammal 6.7m, Reptile 6.1m) trace only to a Facebook infographic (Oct 2026) claiming the APPA 2025-2026 survey and could not be confirmed against APPA's published summary; APPA's own Mar 2026 release gives Dog 71m / Cat 53m. YouGov Jan 2025 (2,223 adults): 48% currently own a dog, 36% a cat — same top 2.

questions.text: What's most people's favorite color?
questions.source: YouGov global color survey (2015, 10 countries on 4 continents): blue is the favorite color in every country surveyed (23-33% of respondents), 8-18 points ahead of second place; second is green, red or purple depending on the country. Joe Hallock's 2003 survey: 42% chose blue.

questions.text: What % of the world's population was infected during the 1918 flu pandemic?
questions.note: About 500 million people — roughly one in three people alive — caught the 1918 flu.
questions.source: CDC, 1918 Pandemic (H1N1 virus): an estimated 500 million people, or one-third of the world's population, became infected

questions.text: What % of Poland's pre-war population died in World War II?
questions.note: About 6 million of Poland's 35 million people died — the highest share of any country in the war.
questions.source: Wikipedia, World War II casualties (by country table): Poland ~5.9-6.0 million deaths of 34.8 million, ~17%

questions.text: What % of Ireland's population died in the Great Famine of 1845-1852?
questions.note: About 1 million of roughly 8.5 million people died; another million emigrated.
questions.source: Wikipedia, Great Famine (Ireland): approximately 1 million deaths from a pre-famine population of about 8.5 million

questions.text: In 1900, what % of the US workforce worked in agriculture?
questions.note: By 2000 it was under 2%.
questions.source: USDA Economic Research Service, The 20th Century Transformation of U.S. Agriculture and Farm Policy (2005): 41% of the workforce in 1900, 1.9% in 2000

questions.text: What % of the US population was born in another country in 1910?
questions.note: 14.7% in 1910 — a record that stood for over a century.
questions.source: US Census Bureau, Historical Census Statistics on the Foreign-Born Population: 14.7% foreign-born in 1910

questions.text: In 1800, what % of children worldwide died before their 5th birthday?
questions.source: Our World in Data (Gapminder & UN IGME), Child mortality: 43.3% of children died before age five in 1800

questions.text: In 1820, what % of the world's adults could read and write?
questions.note: Today it's about 87%.
questions.source: Our World in Data, Literacy: an estimated 12% of the world population aged 15+ was literate in 1820

questions.text: Of all the Allied troops who landed in Normandy on D-Day, what % were American?
questions.note: About 73,000 of the roughly 156,000 troops who landed on June 6, 1944.
questions.source: The National WWII Museum, D-Day: 156,000 Allied troops landed, about 73,000 of them American

questions.text: What % of all the gold ever mined has been mined since 1950?
questions.source: World Gold Council, Above-ground stocks: around two-thirds of all gold ever mined has been mined since 1950

questions.text: What % of Earth's freshwater is locked up in ice caps and glaciers?
questions.source: USGS Water Science School, Where is Earth's Water?: 68.7% of freshwater is in ice caps, glaciers and permanent snow

questions.text: What % of all species that have ever lived on Earth are now extinct?
questions.note: The usual estimate is more than 99%.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Extinction: more than 99% of all species that ever lived are extinct

questions.text: Your brain is about 2% of your body weight. What % of your body's energy does it use?
questions.source: Raichle & Gusnard, PNAS 2002, Appraising the brain's energy budget: the brain is ~2% of body mass but uses ~20% of the body's energy

questions.text: By weight, what % of Earth's crust is oxygen?
questions.note: Silicon is a distant second at about 28%.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica / USGS, abundance of elements in Earth's crust: oxygen ~46% by weight

questions.text: What % of human DNA is identical to chimpanzee DNA?
questions.note: 98.8%, rounded for play.
questions.source: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History, Genetics: humans and chimpanzees share 98.8% of their DNA

questions.text: What % of the world's electricity was generated from coal in 2024?
questions.note: Still the single largest source, though its share keeps falling.
questions.source: Ember, Global Electricity Review 2025 (2024 data): coal 34.4% of global electricity

questions.text: What % of the world's electricity comes from nuclear power?
questions.source: Ember, Global Electricity Review 2025 (2024 data): nuclear 9.0% of global electricity

questions.text: What % of global fossil CO2 emissions come from China?
questions.source: Global Carbon Project, Global Carbon Budget 2023: China 31% of global fossil CO2 emissions (2022)

questions.text: What % of the universe is ordinary matter — everything made of atoms?
questions.note: The rest is dark matter (~27%) and dark energy (~68%).
questions.source: NASA Science, Dark Energy and Dark Matter: normal matter adds up to less than 5% of the universe

questions.text: By mass, what % of the Sun is hydrogen?
questions.note: Most of the rest is helium (~25%).
questions.source: NASA, Sun Fact Sheet / Solar composition: about 73% hydrogen and 25% helium by mass

questions.text: Over time, what % of the Moon's surface can be seen from Earth?
questions.note: A slight wobble (libration) lets us peek around the edges.
questions.source: NASA Science, Moon: thanks to libration, 59% of the lunar surface is visible from Earth over time

questions.text: What % of Apple's revenue came from the iPhone in fiscal 2024?

questions.source: Apple Inc. Form 10-K, fiscal 2024: iPhone net sales $201.2B of total $391.0B

questions.text: What % of Amazon's operating income came from Amazon Web Services in 2024?
questions.note: AWS is about a sixth of Amazon's sales but most of its profit.
questions.source: Amazon.com Form 10-K 2024: AWS operating income $39.8B of total $68.6B

questions.text: What % of Fortune 500 companies are run by a woman CEO?
questions.note: A record 55 in 2025.
questions.source: Fortune, Fortune 500 2025: 55 women CEOs (11%)

questions.text: What % of new US businesses close within their first year?
questions.note: 22.1% for businesses opened in the year to March 2024.
questions.source: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Business Employment Dynamics: 77.9% of establishments opened in the year ended March 2024 were still operating a year later

questions.text: By volume, what % of world trade travels by sea?
questions.source: UNCTAD, Review of Maritime Transport: over 80% of the volume of international trade in goods is carried by sea

questions.source: Netflix Q4 2024 shareholder letter: 301.6M paid memberships, 89.6M in US & Canada

questions.text: What % of Spotify's monthly users pay for Premium?

questions.text: What % of all video game revenue worldwide comes from mobile games?
questions.note: About $93 billion of $188 billion in 2024.
questions.source: Newzoo, Global Games Market Report 2024: mobile $92.6B of $187.7B

questions.text: What % of US GDP is consumer spending?
questions.source: US Bureau of Economic Analysis, NIPA Table 1.1.10: personal consumption expenditures ~68% of GDP

questions.text: What % of the world's wealth is owned by the richest 1% of adults?
questions.note: 47.5% in the latest UBS estimate, rounded for play.
questions.source: UBS / Credit Suisse Global Wealth Report (2023 data, via inequality.org): the top 1% of adults hold 47.5% of global household wealth

questions.text: By value, what % of all US cash in circulation is in $100 bills?
questions.source: Federal Reserve (FRED series CURRVAL100): $100 notes ~$1.9 trillion of ~$2.3 trillion total currency in circulation, 2024

questions.text: What % of the world's central bank currency reserves are held in US dollars?
questions.note: 57.8% at the end of 2024; the euro is second at about 20%.
questions.source: IMF, Currency Composition of Official Foreign Exchange Reserves (COFER), Q4 2024

questions.text: What % of the world's population lives in India and China combined?
questions.note: About 2.9 billion of 8.2 billion people.
questions.source: United Nations, World Population Prospects 2024

questions.text: What % of Africa's population is under 25?
questions.source: United Nations DESA, World Population Prospects 2024: about 60% of Africa's population is under age 25

questions.text: What % of Australians live in the eight state and territory capital cities?
questions.source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Regional Population 2022-23: 67% of Australians live in capital cities

questions.text: What % of the world's land area is Russia?
questions.note: 17.1 million of about 149 million square kilometres.
questions.source: CIA World Factbook: Russia 17.1M km²; world land area 148.9M km²

questions.text: What % of the Amazon rainforest lies in Brazil?
questions.source: WWF, Amazon facts: about 60% of the Amazon rainforest is in Brazil

questions.text: What % of Earth's atmosphere is argon?
questions.note: More than carbon dioxide by a factor of about twenty.
questions.source: NASA Earth Fact Sheet: argon 9,340 ppm (0.93%) of the atmosphere

questions.text: What % of Earth's atmosphere is carbon dioxide?
questions.note: About 423 ppm in 2024 — small, but up by half since the 1700s.
questions.source: NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory, Trends in atmospheric CO2: 2024 global annual mean ~423 ppm (0.04%)

questions.text: What % of Earth's mass is its oceans?
questions.note: About 1.4 × 10²¹ kg of seawater on a 6 × 10²⁴ kg planet.
questions.source: USGS ocean volume (~1.33 billion km³ of seawater ≈ 1.4×10²¹ kg) divided by Earth's mass (5.97×10²⁴ kg, NASA Earth Fact Sheet)

questions.text: What % of the human genome is made of genes that code for proteins?
questions.note: About 1%; much of the rest regulates those genes.
questions.source: National Human Genome Research Institute: only about 1 percent of DNA is made up of protein-coding genes

questions.text: Of everyone who has ever been born, what % is alive today?
questions.note: About 8 billion of roughly 117 billion humans ever born.
questions.source: Population Reference Bureau, How Many People Have Ever Lived on Earth? (2022): ~117 billion ever born

questions.text: What % of Best Picture Oscar winners were directed by a woman?
questions.note: Three of 97: The Hurt Locker, Nomadland and CODA.
questions.source: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, Oscars database: Best Picture winners through the 97th Academy Awards (2025)
